text:
Predicates:
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
MountainRange(x) ::: x is a mountain range.
LocatedIn(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
Mine(x) ::: x is a mine.
Donated(x) ::: x was donated.
In(x, y) ::: x is in y.

Premises:
PicurisMountains(x) ∧ MountainRange(x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, newMexico) ∨ LocatedIn(x, texas) ::: The Picuris Mountains are a mountain range in New Mexico or Texas.
Visited(juanDeOnate, x) ∧ MountainRange(x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, y) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.
Mine(hinghamPegmatiteMine) ∧ LocatedIn(hinghamPegmatiteMine, x) ∧ MountainRange(x) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine, located in the Picuris Mountains, was donated.
Donated(hinghamPegmatiteMine) ::: The mine was donated.
∀x (Mine(x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, y) ∧ y = texas) → ¬Donated(x) ::: There are no mountain ranges in Texas with donated mines.

Conclusion:
Visited(juanDeOnate, x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, newMexico) ::: Juan de Onate visited a mountain range in New Mexico.
